analysis.title: Intel: Downgrade to Neutral, turnaround pushed out on PC/supply headwinds
key_insights: BofA downgrades INTC to Neutral from Buy (C-2-9 from C-1-9) and cuts the price objective to $100 from $145. Price at publication was $92.07.
Reasons for the downgrade: not enough traction with external foundry customers, and a sharp drop in PC shipments (down 25-30% QoQ in Q4, with further inventory correction expected in 1H27).

Data center CPU demand is rising with agentic AI, but supply is tight (substrate) and Intel's products are not yet technically competitive against AMD and ARM-based rivals that are growing 2x-4x faster.
BofA acknowledges Intel's longer-term ability to build a competitive domestic foundry. Any sign of external customer traction could drive a recovery in a relatively under-owned stock.
BofA lowers CY27/28E EPS by 16%/4% to $1.69/$2.79. CY26E EPS rises slightly to $1.49 from $1.47.
The $100 PO applies about 20x P/E to CY30E EPS power of $5.89, discounted back to CY28. The prior $145 PO used about 29x on $6.14. Long-term EPS power drops to $5-$6 from $6-$7.
The $100 PO implies about a $550bn market cap: $450bn for Products (roughly half of AMD's market cap) and about $100bn for the emerging Foundry.
At TSMC's roughly 11x price/sales, a $100bn Foundry valuation implies about $8-10bn of external business. That could eventually reach 8-10% of the roughly $380bn wafer foundry TAM.
Q3 results: sales of $16.5bn were in line with the Street (-0.2% vs consensus). Non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 beat consensus by $0.11, helped by stronger server CPU trends.
Q3 segment results: DCAI revenue of $7.3bn beat the Street by 11.1% (+77.8% YoY). CCPG revenue of $8.1bn missed by 8.9%. Non-GAAP gross margin was 44.1% and operating margin 19.6%.

Q4 guidance is below the Street on sales and EPS. Sales are guided to $15.5bn vs the Street's $17.05bn. Non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 38.0% vs the Street's 42.8%. EPS is guided to $0.25 vs the Street's $0.43.
BofA's new 4Q26E has CCPG revenue falling 25.3% QoQ to $6.05bn while DCAI rises 16.1% QoQ to $8.49bn. CY27E sales are cut 8% to $67.1bn, and 1Q27E EPS falls to $0.24 from $0.40.

Read-across: PC weakness could weigh on AMD (up to a $750mn PC headwind, offset by $500mn+ of strong server CPU revenue). AMD reports next week, with consensus calling for flat client PC into Q4 vs Intel down 25-30%. The AMD Helios/MI ramp could offset it.

Intel's data center strength is positive for AI semis NVDA, AVGO and MRVL. Spending intentions (CY27 growth, with a rising equipment mix) are positive for semicaps, especially KLAC, lithography, AMAT and LRCX.

Foundry opportunities BofA lists but does not yet model: Apple M-Series wafers, MediaTek TPU packaging, Terafab IP/packaging and other ARM-based server CPUs. The recent CDNS 14A collaboration announcement makes these more possible.
Balance sheet: total cash rose to $54.0bn in Sep-26 and net cash was $3.9bn ($0.73 per share), vs a net debt of $20.8bn the prior quarter. Free cash flow was $1.86bn in Q3.
Capex is forecast to rise to $26.0bn in 2027E and $30.4bn in 2028E. BofA expects FCF of -$2.6bn in 2027E and $1.7bn in 2028E, and no net cash position through CY28E.

market_movers.rationale: Downgraded from Buy with PO cut to $145 to $100. Weak PC shipments, tight substrate supply and limited external foundry traction push out the turnaround.

sector_views.rationale: Intel's data center CPU strength is offset by a PC unit decline and supply constraints. The read-across is positive for AI semis and semicaps and slightly negative for AMD.

earnings_insights: INTC Q3 2026 reported 10/30: non-GAAP EPS (ex-SBC) $0.52 vs Street $0.41 (+$0.11) and BofA est $0.37. Revenue $16.51bn non-GAAP vs Street $16.54bn.
INTC Q4 2026 guidance: revenue about $15.5bn, non-GAAP gross margin about 38.0%, non-GAAP EPS $0.25. Street estimates before the guide were revenue $17.05bn, gross margin 42.8% and EPS $0.43.
BofA est EPS (non-GAAP, ex-SBC): CY26E $1.49 (prior $1.47), CY27E $1.69 (prior $2.01), CY28E $2.79 (prior $2.92). Bloomberg consensus is $1.55/$2.12/$3.20.
BofA est revenue: CY26E $61.7bn (prior $62.9bn), CY27E $67.1bn (prior $73.1bn), CY28E $80.4bn (prior $84.7bn).
AMD reports next week. BofA flags up to a $750mn PC headwind, offset by $500mn+ of server CPU revenue. Consensus has AMD client PC flat into Q4.
risk_factors: PC unit shipments down 25-30% QoQ in Q4, with further inventory correction expected in 1H27.
Tight substrate supply constrains data center CPU growth.
Intel products are not yet technically competitive against AMD and ARM-based rivals growing 2x-4x faster.
Higher capex pressures free cash flow in the near to medium term.

tension_points.bull_case: Data center CPU is doing well in a rising agentic tide (DCAI revenue +77.8% YoY in Q3). Any external foundry traction on 18A-P/14A could drive a recovery in a relatively under-owned stock.
tension_points.bear_case: Q4 PC shipments are down 25-30% QoQ, substrate supply is tight, and products lag AMD and ARM-based rivals growing 2x-4x faster. External foundry traction has not yet been communicated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An announcement of external customer traction on 18A-P/14A would be the upside trigger for the stock.
